DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card says family-config / RosDriver. The pinned ROS node has no stop (only the /cmd_vel subscription and a 1 s age check for ROS commands, mvsim_node.cpp:525-540, 934-942), so the package drives MVSim's own ZMQ/protobuf services as a direct Driver over the upstream client's callService member; its native is the pybind11 binding of mvsim::Client (generated Client.cpp:24-87), resolved by the new G7 rule for pybind: selectors. SCOPE: one vehicle (option vehicle, default r1 as in mvsim-teleop.py:40 and the tutorial worlds): x-cap.mrpt.mvsim_controller_twist.v1 through set_controller_twist (vx in m/s, wz in rad/s, ControllerBase.h:44-54; the receipt completes only when MVSim answers that the controller accepted the setpoint and reports that setpoint) and x-cap.mrpt.mvsim_pose.v1 through get_pose. The pose read has a side effect: get_pose makes the next simulation step reset the vehicle's own hadCollision flag (World_services.cpp:115-120, World_simul.cpp:260-269), which the ROS node's collision topic also reads and resets (mvsim_node.cpp:1120-1130); the in_collision it reports comes from a record the step only adds to (World_simul.cpp:254-256). NOT COVERED: set_pose, shutdown, the light services, MVSim topics, the ROS node surface, other vehicles and objects.

E-STOP: a zero twist through set_controller_twist, which MVSim applies under its simulation-step lock and answers with success only when the controller accepted it (World_services.cpp:124-170): zero velocity is commanded, not measured braking (twist_ideal sets the twist at once; twist_pid and Ackermann controllers slow the vehicle over time). A raw-force or trajectory controller refuses twist commands (the ControllerBase default; the trajectory controller keeps following its path), and the e-stop then stays unreached with the latch held. ROS cmd_vel, the GUI teleop and other MVSim clients are not fenced and can command the vehicle again. RISK R2 (device and twist action): velocity setpoints are mobile-base transit, R2 in the hazard table of MHS/spec/04-safety.md (handoff rule 13), as in the comparable simulated mobile-base packages, although MVSim has no hardware path; the card floor is R0 (the first draft said R0; corrected after the round-1 review). LIMITS: vx and wz are operator_required (MVSim states no bound for a twist setpoint); site-limits.example.json is example operator data for the gate's conformance run.

LIVE ROUTE: sim.py builds mvsim_wire.MvsimServiceClient, the package's own client with its own declared dependency (pyzmq in driver.lock.json install; never an SDK dependency); the package encodes MVSim's protobuf messages itself (mvsim_wire.py, standard library, field numbers from modules/msgs/proto). The upstream Python client is not used because its calls wait on ZMQ without a timeout (common.cpp:63-73) in a binding that does not release the GIL (generated Client.cpp:74-87), so a silent simulator could stall the whole process, e-stop included. Every call of this client is bounded (timeout_s, default 2 s): an unanswered setpoint is an unknown outcome, an unanswered stop an unreached safe state. It calls only set_controller_twist and get_pose and passes on only their own answer types or a GenericAnswer whose success is false (Client.cpp:565-580), so no other message reads as an accepted zero twist; it connects to the configured host at the port the server reports for a service (MVSim reports its wildcard bind, Client.cpp:166-167, 462), never to a host the server names, where the upstream client connects verbatim (Client.cpp:775, 783). Its envelope follows mvsim::sendMessage (common.cpp:20-46) with MRPT's little-endian length-prefixed strings, MRPT behaviour outside the clone. It has not been run against an MVSim server.

FAKE: answers set_controller_twist and get_pose as World does at the pin (unknown object, refused twist, success), from placeholder state (vehicle r1, a fixed pose, the twist_ideal response); its answers are encoded independently of the package's request encoder, and byte vectors in test_driver.py pin the encoding to the .proto field numbers. test_driver.py: 28 cases (check_driver kept), including the bounded client against a stand-in of the pyzmq calls it makes (answer types, endpoint host, unknown services).
